title: Visually styled heading is absent from the heading list
description: The What happens next title is a paragraph styled to look like a heading. It looks correct but does not appear in the heading list or the accessibility tree's heading navigation.
component: What happens next section title (variant A)

relatedElements.note: A real h3 in the control.

expectedBehaviour: Text that acts as a heading uses a heading element so it appears in the heading list.
actualBehaviour: The title is a p element with heading-like styling and no heading semantics.
userImpact: Screen-reader users who navigate by heading miss the section entirely.

observed.note: Page-level axe run with tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and best-practice. No violation was reported for this page in its default state; the control on the same page also passes.

detection.note: Visual review alone accepts the styled paragraph; the accessibility tree exposes the missing heading.

manualTests: Open the headings list for the page and look for What happens next.

assistiveTechnologyTests.procedure: Navigate to the target with the VoiceOver rotor and confirm what is announced.

assertions: No heading named What happens next exists in variant A, while variant B exposes an h3.
tests: tests/subtle-defects.spec.js: keeps the visual-only heading out of the heading list in variant A

reviewStatus.note: A Playwright regression test preserves the defective behaviour and its control. That is automated reproduction, not a manual or assistive-technology observation.
